newsitem.title: FRANCE: French health insurance fund to make savings.
newsitem.headline: French health insurance fund to make savings.

text.p: France's national health insurance fund said on Tuesday that it proposed to save four billion francs a year by cutting the price of some medical procedures and promoting the use of generic medecines.

The Caisse Nationale d'Assurance Maladie des Travailleurs Salaries (CNAMTS) said the plans were put forward by its health insurance commission, which met at the request of Labour Minister Jacques Barrot.

It proposed "measures...which take account of technological changes and favour responsibility on the part of medical professionals and which will have an expected economic impact of about four billion francs in a full year," Jean-Marie Spaeth, new head of the CNAMTS said in a statement.
The statement gave no details of savings.

The CNAMTS also said it would distribute before the end of the year a guide to generic medecines to encourage doctors to prescribe the cheaper medicines. Spaeth said the new measures would not have an impact on insured people as most of the cost would be borne by medical professionals.
